headline: Organic growth holds and margins expand
summary_short: Revenue rose 3% to $4,101M with 6% organic growth, and adjusted EPS grew 10% to $3.36. Aon expects the USI acquisition to close in the fourth quarter of 2026.
summary_long: Organic growth was 7% in Commercial Risk, 7% in Reinsurance, 6% in Health and 4% in Wealth. Divestitures, mainly the NFP Wealth sale, cut reported revenue growth by 3 points. Operating expenses rose 3%, including $93M of Accelerating Aon United program costs. No shares were repurchased; about $7.7B of authorization remains. Debt repayment is the priority after USI closes, targeting 2.8x-3.0x leverage in roughly 24 months.
confidence_notes: Adjusted EPS, adjusted margin, organic growth and free cash flow are non-GAAP measures. Free cash flow delta is the release's own comparison.

drivers.explanation: Net new business and strong retention drove 6% organic growth, partly offset by a 3% drag from divestitures including NFP Wealth and Stroz Friedberg.
Organic growth plus $20M of net restructuring savings and lower expenses from the NFP Wealth sale, partly offset by growth investments.
Lower share count of 213.0M versus 216.7M and a lower effective tax rate of 20.6% supported EPS growth.
CEO says AI-enabled analytics and capital solutions are advancing the strategy and he sees significant momentum into the fourth quarter.
